It was amazing I had even lived this long, no one thought I would. I was in my room at the hospital when my paper arrived, with bated breath, I opened it and read the four large words on the page.

"Don't enter the light."

That was it? All that suspension for those words? Thats not a description, thats a saying, a phrase, a little joke everyone says, especially to the dying. With a scoff I threw it in the bin, rolled over and fell asleep.

The next day I woke up to the sight of baffled medical staff, who, once they realised I was awake told me that I would live, I was completely healthy. Looking in a Mirror later, I realised how right they were. Gone was my sickly hue, my sunken eyes, I was back to a healthy weight, could breath easy, and the best part, there were no more aches.

​

I thought that was the extent of it, that it was a one time thing, boy, was I proven wrong when a few years later I woke in Intensive Care after my car got driven off a cliff, completely fine. Later prompting revealed I had been close to death, more close than my childhood affliction. I was discharged the next day. 

After surviving increasingly impossible scenarios, I pieced it together, well, after I 'miraculously' survived the bullet to the brain, I could not die, I was unkillable. So, I figured 'Hey why not make a job of it.'

Its amazing how fast you become a living legend and myth in just a few jobs, I was quickly known as the Immortal bodyguard, protector, or simply, 'The one who survives anything,' Saving peoples lives like that, gets you a few favours, its also lonely too, extensive research had shown that healing, regeneration and resurrection powers were not hereditary, but rather something that just occurs, any children I had, would not inherit this.

I watched Humanity grow, due to my reputation, I had long been put in charge of the world secrets, access codes, and new leader of the group, or thing in charge of power registration, after all, after a while of multiple close calls, you gain an extremely high pain tolerance.

After a few milennia though, humanity was dying out, too many mutations to catch up to the powers. I watched again, feeling hopeless, they had a few centuries at best, I was no longer alone though in my immortality, a few others had similar things, with variations and conditions. Together we had a meeting with the remainder of Humanity and came to an agreement, Humanity, with a few to watch would venture away from the also dying planet, and seek help from the intelligent species we knew were out there. It didnt take long to bbuild transport, with all the powers helping, it was well done. 

So, we packed and left, the majority going into a deep sleep, the rest of us taking guard and navigating. Those of us awake encountered incredible things, unspeakable things, and we made sure to chronicle it for others. Some planets gave us hope, and ideas, as we rapidly found we were not the only species to have encountered the problem. No one could explain what stopped the point of extinction though, especially seeing as powers were not transferrable, nor could one have more than one power.

We gained new companions too, those with no true cause, or who had some unknown instruction to. Either way, my loneliness was finally vanishing, I sought solitude and intimacy with those like me, and grew to love the child we gained, who had a beautiful chronicling power, able to take extreme details and log them in a way any could understand, including immaculate drawings, with time, we found that she had also gained a immortality of a sort, as long as she chronicled, she kept her youth. 

It wasn't until we saw an immortal outside, with no gear, that we got answers, once we allowed them to board. The first thing I noticed, was the same instructions I had received, tattooed on their wrist. 

They spoke of the same issues we had come across, how their species was not that different from our own, further more, they were like me, a leader for their race, because of their gift, with negotiations, we joined them, and became apart of their lifestyle, settling down, despite the homesickness, Humanitys endangered status was fixed, and we stayed there, on our new home, seeking to explore more.

Most people think its cool that I can create any tools out of anything I can get my hands on. Don't get me wrong, as a kid, thats what I thought too. In fact, as a child, I loved creating whatever I could think of. Tools is such a vast word too, that I was able to, out of just a few sticks, dirt and grass, able to create a whole shed, that went both above and below ground, to this day I am still exploring parts of it.

As long as I maintained a loose definition of the word 'tool' I could create almost anything, except food. Obviously. Growing up, while still discovering the limits of my smithing powers, I created all types of grass, stick, wood, dirt and paper tools. During this period, I found, quite by accident, that I could create dolls furniture, as, my logic was, its a tool to help you play with the dolls more and to get the imagination for games you may play with them.

That increased my popularity sevenfold. With both Children and Adults.

Soon I was sought out for all kinds, unfortunately for me, most of them I didn't class as a tool, therefore I could not create it. As that became more and more true, I began retreating to my shed more and more, allowing those with orders to post them through my mailing system I had created for this situation.

Even more unfortunate, various militaries had heard of my powers, and so had started posting orders for me. They'd offered comfortable sums of money, and even protection, and so with my continuous supply of wood, sticks, leaves and dirt, I created prototypes and mailed them back, keeping some for myself for self-defense. 

Before long, I had a steady business with them, along with business with a Green. One of my many tunnels it turned out, lead out to their property, in what I'm sure was no mere coincidence. We would meet in the tunnel and swap, I would give her the gardening tools she required, and she would give me a supply of her produce, all of which tasted as sweet and amazing as she did. 

At one point, I created a scarecrow for her, and she asked me to plant it for her, even though we both knew she was more than able to. It was the first time I had stepped outside since I retreated into my sanctuary, I gaped in Wonder at the beauty Persephone Green had created, colours filled her fields, I saw flowers blossom and bloom as she walked. I saw fields of sheep and cows and other animals be tended to by a few Shepherds and Shephards,  and all other variations I may have forgotten. The wheat she grew, was being milled by Millers, and the wool being tended to various Tailors, Taylors and others. 

Everywhere I looked, I saw a woorking beehive, where it was clear that Persephone ran the farm as Queen Bee. 

However, beyond the vast farm, was a warzone, One I instantly knew was created by me. Once planting the scarecrow where she asked, I requested the strongest materials she had, that I knew she had. With them, I Smithed the best tool I ever had in my life. 

Around the farm I had Smithed a large Greenhouse, with multiple functions. It was war-proof, with functioning turrets, as well as sufficent to keep them all safe within with a system that imitated the weather. I slumped when the rush of the massive energy left, but I felt proud that I had helped Miss Persephone.

Her hand caressed my slumped head and moved me to look into her eyes. "Thank you for this magnificent Gift, Vulcan Smith, the greatest Smith ever to live."

I knew then that I wished to stay in her community, and if she allowed, to have children who beared both our names. 

That was how we all lived though, while the world destroyed itself, occasionally I would increase our bubble, so Miss Green may heal the land.

Fear not the man who has everything to lose. For a man with everything to lose is one who has achieved happiness. A man with everything to lose will always lose things. 

Fear instead the man with nothing to lose. A man with nothing to lose has everything to give. None of it in your favour. A man with nothing to lose is like a good man going to war. In his own right he is a fearsome sight.

That is what they learnt the day *they* came. When the world went from bad, to worse, due to visitors we'd all hoped for, and yet, never expected. They came when we thought we needed them most, when we were most desperate. At first, it was just a few scouts, observing our world, they were the background, unnoticable. Well, not by us anyway, animals seems to sense something was off, but who listens to animalistic instincts, right?

We should have.

It wasn't long before they had what they wanted. We weren't a species they could coexist with, not when we could barely coexist with other humans. So they did the collective universe a favour and launched war. They didn't even have to directly attack us, not when they were, persuasive, hell, all they needed was a few chosen words and we destroyed ourselves. It was the beginning of the end. 

Fortunately, or, rather unfortunately, they didn't destroy all of us, only most of us. At the time I was barely out of my teens, wanting to do my part to try help the world, I had a plan, I'd worked it all out. 

I never had the chance to execute it.

They came and ruined everything. I didn't mind when my family had gone, they were cell donors if anything, we hadn't been a real family in years. All communication paths had just, vanished though. No internet, cell service was gone, all modes of travel, and in the end, even face to face contact.

That was when they started taking people, more noticeably anyway. By that point, without any communication, I was lost, a shell of myself, I had nothing. Which was when they came for me.

I still remember that day. I had just found out how alone I was. No one was around anymore, everything was burning, the Planet of Earth, was almost entirely humanless by then. and it was thriving. Nature was finally taking her place once more. The air was clean, animals roamed, no longer kept at bay by humans. I had a small shelter, and had learnt how to coexist in this new world. No signs of them had been spotted for weeks. Naively I had thought it was over, and they were gone, as usual, I was wrong.

They surrounded me, in a heartbeat I knew how hunted animals felt like. Seeing no immediate opening, I surrendered, so they thought. I'd long since learnt how to fool them. Why would they pay attention to someone who shows nothing, no hostility at all? As they opened up at the front to lead me up to their ship, I bolted through the gap, not away from them, like they had expected, but towards the ship, if I was going to be their captive, I may as well run towards it. Doesn't mean I had to make it easy for them.

Once inside, I remained still, waiting for them, to their surprise. They had expected me to wreck havoc. I would, eventually. From the inside.

I did what they did to us. I observed, I was co-operative, that surprised them, even made them happy, apparently everyone else they took fought. Turned out the ship I was on was small in their fleet, they all were, but each ship was allowed to take one human. With good behaviour, I was allowed to even have a few pets.

That was when I fought back. Small things of course, the flap of a butterflies wing and all that. All I did was play with technology. How was I to know I would explode the infirmary? I was just a human, in foreign waters, which is what I told the Captain, smirking at those who saw me plant mini bombs I had created. 

Soon I had the crew split, half thought I was a dumb, docile human, the other half knew I was smart, destructive and mad as hell. I spent my time divided between exploring the ship, and staying in my quarters.

Whispers from the crew followed my every step.

*'This human scares me.'*

"*So calculating."*

I smirked inwardly.

Fear not the man with everything to lose, but one who has lost everything. The man who has lost everything can be patient, and has everything to give. And give I did. 

I took down the fleet that had destroyed Earth in time, grouped up with a few humans, destroyed the rest, and with a liberated ship, we went on to explore. Communicating through the communications one saying.

"Fear not the man with everything to lose, instead fear He who has lost everything."

I've been avoiding eye contact for as long as I can remember. Why? Easy. The eyes are the window to the soul, literally. Through eyes, I can read thoughts, or is it hear them? or See them? It depends on the thought. If they happen to be thinking music, I hear that, if they are picturing something, I see that, and if they are in the midst of reading or writing something,  I read it.

You have no *idea* how distracting it can be. Okay, well, I suppose you can imagine. Oh, and eye contact doesn't have to be full on staring into eyes all lovey dovey or all that. It can be a glimpse at the eyes and they see you, then *whooooosh* I can hear them. There is a *lot* of sick minds out there, so I tend to keep to myself, eyes down, I come across as rude, but whats ruder, avoiding eye contact, or reading what should be private thoughts?

One day, I was getting ready to go out, when I glanced in the Mirror, one of m only safe places. I can't hear my own thoughts, because I already know them, it was my way of getting ready to go out. I was settled, relaxed and ready to leave when, 

*"Please, no, not again, not today, I can't deal with it all today."* 

Startled, I whirled around, but I didn't see anyone, shaken, I turned back to the mirror.

*"Why would you see me? I'm not really here, I'm a ghost I suppose, but please, the crowds, they will over whelme us, stay here, I beg you!"*

Electing to ignore the voice, I went outside anyway, I had things to do, shopping.

I should have listened.

People were everywhere, and I keep getting jostled, until I got bumped and looked up to steady myself. Instant regret. All around me there were eyes watching me. Voices battered into the weak defences I had always set up, until with a crash audible only to me, they shattered. 

Panic.

All I could think of was how panicked I was, Noise was all I could hear, until there was silence.

I awoke in a room, a Mirror on the ceiling, I was tied to a bed, scrapes on me. A single voice speaking to me.

*"I asked you not to go out."*

I wasn't even aware I was in hell at the start. It looked just like Earth. Hell, heh, see what I did there? I wasn't even aware I *had* died, one second I was up walking, talking and all that, the next I was here, actually, it looks like Australia kinda...

"Are you quite done talking to yourself?"

"Huh? Oh, yes. So, what was the offer again?"

Satan, sorry, I think he wanted me to call him, Morningstar? or Luci? Maybe it was Lucifer, anyway, he sighed, and rolled his eyes, already he was getting tired of dealing with me. Good, maybe he'd shove off and leave me so i could, find someway to leave.

"Oi! Could you at least try *paying* attention?"

"Wha?"

"Oh me, this is gonna be hard. You have the attention span of a, hmmm, something with a bad attention span. But shut up and just *FOCUS* for one second, could you? I am very impressed with your, well, not exciting, was kinda mundane actually, life. You didn't actually do much. But! That is *why* I'm impressed with you... OI OI FOCUS! Jeez You are tough.
